newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Pressured vs US.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Pressured vs US.

text.p: The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond spread remained under pressure, slipping briefly through 100 basis basis points, as the local market failed to build on an early U.S.-inspired rally in slow trading.
The absence of any key data, a U.S. holiday for Presidents Day and caution ahead of the Reserve Bank's quarterly bulletin ensured that local interest was kept to a minimum.

However, some anaylsts feel there is room for this spread to contract again given the still modest growth outlook on inflation, the prospect of further fiscal tightening in the May budget and as the domestic economy is out of sync with the U.S..

"There's scope to retest the lows of a few weeks ago at the 70 level. We're seeing a bit of interest from some U.S. investors and they are pretty comfortable with the Australian story," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank
The U.S. market rallied on a 0.3 percent fall in the U.S. PPI for January on Friday, the first drop since October 1995.
This also buoyed the Canadian market which faces its federal budget on Tuesday, while, like Australia, New Zealand bonds gave up some of there early firm advance.
